stories.headline: Baltic defense ministers sign military mobility agreement in Tallinn
stories.summary: Defense Minister Hanno Pevkur hosted Latvian and Lithuanian defense ministers for signing of joint military mobility agreement to simplify cross-border movement of forces. The ministers also discussed Baltic defense cooperation, NATO, and Ukraine support.

stories.headline: Tsahkna pushes EU-wide entry ban for Russian war veterans
stories.summary: Foreign Minister Margus Tsahkna proposed EU-wide entry ban for Russian soldiers who fought in Ukraine, stating 'there can be no path from Bucha to Brussels.' He raised the issue at EU foreign ministers meeting, citing security concerns about nearly one million Russian combatants.

stories.headline: Pevkur presents defense development plan to parliament
stories.summary: Defense Minister Hanno Pevkur outlined Estonia's defense development plan to 2035 to parliament's defense committee, promising to submit it to government by April. The plan includes naval modernization, air defense improvements, and expanding active personnel by 500-600 people over ten years.

stories.headline: Estonia allocates €400,000 humanitarian aid to Ukraine
stories.summary: Foreign Minister Tsahkna announced new humanitarian aid package for Ukraine, stating that Putin uses cold and darkness as weapons against Ukrainians. Estonia also responded to Russian strike on Zaporizhzhia maternity hospital, emphasizing continued support for Ukraine.

stories.headline: Estonia weighs eastern border closure after Russian crossing
stories.summary: Foreign Minister Tsahkna said full closure of Estonia's eastern border remains an option after Russia's illegal border crossing last month. The government has not yet seen a direct security threat requiring closure but considers it a possible pressure measure.

articles.title: Estonia weighs possible eastern border closure after Russia crossing

stories.headline: Kaitseliit recognizes best members and conducts training exercises
stories.summary: Estonian Defence League held annual recognition ceremony in Tallinn, naming year's best defence league member and youth leaders. Separately, defence league units conducted training exercises, including in school buildings and various locations.
